tells.1: Labeled “Options:” list plus a scripted yes-or-Corvane closer reads like a decision form.
tells.2: The mirrored “if you’re happy / if you’d rather” close is a little too neatly balanced.
tells.3: One flattened paragraph ending in a bare “Reply yes to confirm” command.
tells.4: Looks like a tightened edit of the same template: added comma, dropped “can you,” clipped sign-off.

reason: Version 2 paces the ask, the saving, and the recommendation like a colleague typing in Slack, while 1 and 4 lean on the same tidy options-and-reply template and 3 compresses it into a blunt block.
